questions.question: You need to enable self-service password reset (SSPR) only for the members of a group named Pilot. What should you configure on the Properties page of Password reset?

options.text: Set Self service password reset enabled to Selected and select the Pilot group
options.why: Correct. Selected applies SSPR to one chosen group.

options.text: Set Self service password reset enabled to All
options.why: All enables SSPR for every user in the tenant.

options.text: Set Self service password reset enabled to None and add Pilot as an exception
options.why: None disables SSPR and has no exception list.

options.text: Assign the Password Administrator role to the Pilot group
options.why: This role lets members reset other users’ passwords; it does not enable SSPR for them.

questions.explanation: The Selected option supports one group. Nest groups within it or use All for broader scope.

questions.question: Users must verify their identity with two different methods before they can reset their password by using SSPR. What should you configure?

options.text: Number of methods required to reset set to 2
options.why: Correct. This requires two registered methods during reset.

options.text: Number of days before users are asked to re-confirm their authentication information set to 2
options.why: This controls how often users reconfirm registration, not how many methods are required.

options.text: Require users to register when signing in set to Yes
options.why: This prompts registration but does not set the number of methods required.

options.text: Notify users on password resets set to Yes
options.why: Notifications inform users after a reset; they do not add verification.

questions.explanation: The Authentication methods page of Password reset sets the number of methods required (1 or 2) and the allowed methods.

questions.question: SSPR is enabled for all users. Synchronized users report that new passwords set through SSPR do not work when they sign in to on-premises domain-joined computers. What should you configure?

options.text: Password writeback in Microsoft Entra Connect and on the On-premises integration page
options.why: Correct. Writeback sends cloud password changes to on-premises Active Directory.

options.text: Security questions as an authentication method
options.why: Authentication methods do not synchronize passwords to on-premises.

options.text: Number of methods required to reset set to 1
options.why: The number of methods does not affect on-premises passwords.

options.text: A dynamic group for synchronized users
options.why: Group membership does not write passwords back to Active Directory.

questions.explanation: Password writeback requires Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync and Microsoft Entra ID P1.

questions.question: SSPR is set to Selected for Group1 with two methods required. User1 is a member of Group1 and registered only an email address. What happens when User1 attempts to reset their password?

options.text: The reset fails until User1 registers another allowed method
options.why: Correct. User1 must pass the required number of registered methods.

options.text: The reset succeeds by using email only
options.why: Two methods are required by the policy.

options.text: The reset succeeds because User1 is a member of Group1
options.why: Group membership places User1 in scope, but the method requirement still applies.

options.text: An administrator approval request is sent automatically
options.why: SSPR does not include an approval workflow.

questions.explanation: Users must be in scope and have registered at least the required number of allowed methods.

questions.question: Which two statements about SSPR for administrator accounts are true? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Administrators are enabled for SSPR regardless of the Selected or All setting
options.why: Correct. The administrator reset policy is always enabled.

options.text: Administrators must use two authentication methods to reset
options.why: Correct. The administrator policy requires two methods.

options.text: Administrators can use security questions as one of their methods
options.why: Security questions are not available to administrator accounts.

options.text: Administrators are excluded from SSPR when the setting is None
options.why: The administrator policy applies even when SSPR is set to None for users.

questions.explanation: Microsoft enforces a stronger two-gate policy for administrator roles and does not allow security questions.
